body:
This preserves two completed Ultra investigations with their actual status: the earlier HIP acquisition limits (FM/N815) and the new compact quantum-response certificate campaign (FN/N816). Neither establishes a new physical capability or a complete-resource advantage.

The response packet derives a conditional exact local-MPS completion algorithm, verifies finite AKLT certificates through compact transfer contractions, and preserves the decisive matched comparison: an acquired four-spin patch gap gives a tighter six-site response interval than the proposed dual. All-size feasibility, historical priority, robust material-input acquisition and useful advantage remain open. The older HIP packet retains its pressure/isotope countermodels and prior-art failures without restarting that research direction.

Committed source bytes are pinned to separate Ultra commits `788beabca49c9821a86c8237b1328a53313a22c5` and `e7ae999e957d70f98ccb9bd789c3eeb6c8229d30`. Readable core files, selected deterministic archives, source comparisons, exact statuses and open gates are included. Raw downloads and installed runtimes omitted from this intake are explicitly recorded; the full Ultra packet is separately versioned.

Validation: intake preservation/wiring validators, generated access freshness, frontier fixtures, exact new-only checkpoint validation and source-byte comparisons. The source packet also contains root copy-first scientific replays of the exact N6 interval, compact N6/N12 completion, narrow obstruction, virtual identity and defeating comparator. These checks have their stated integrity/finite-computation scope; no external scientific review or experimental validation is asserted.

Global checkpoint validation still fails on three inherited unsupported-schema records. Their bytes and ancestry are preserved; only the new FM/FN handoffs are individually validated. This failure is reported, not treated as a pass.

The base is current `main` at `ace0cfc4437fe91c20ccd24d69e0ee4bb335e871`. Draft PR #83 was checked separately at `ae7837e6c71716c40d247338e3a77de34e6e4928`; its FL/N812–N814 allocation is respected. This draft uses FM/FN and N815/N816. It will need reconciliation and regenerated access if the shared base or concurrent intake changes before merge.
